english.title: Religiously aggravated criminal damage
english.standardoffencewording:
On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..) without lawful excuse,

(A)_[destroyed **(..SPECIFY PROPERTY..)]_
(B)_[damaged **(..SPECIFY PROPERTY..)]_

(C)_[to the value of **(..SPECIFY VALUE..)]_
(D)_[to a value unknown]_

belonging to **(..SPECIFY NAME..) intending to destroy or damage such property or being reckless as to whether such property would be destroyed or damaged which was religiously aggravated in accordance with section 28 of the Crime and Disorder Act 1998
english.legislation: Contrary to section 30(1) and (2) of the Crime and Disorder Act 1998.
english.pointstoprove:
date and location
without lawful excuse destroyed/damaged property

the offence was religiously aggravated

english.notes:
This CJS Code and Standard Offence Wording is OBSOLETE. Now see CJS Code CD98074 and Offence Wording H10011.

(i) where the specific date of the offence is not known, the charge should read: "...on a date between X and Y...". where 'X' is the last date before the first date on which the offence could have occurred, and 'Y' is the first date after the last date it could have occurred.
(e.g. a factory closes Friday evening to Monday morning. It is broken into over the weekend. The charge should read: "...on a date between X (Thursday's date) and Y (Tuesday's date)...".)
(ii) The option to return an alternative verdict of guilty of the basic offence is NOT available in the magistrates court, therefore the basic offence should be charged in addition to the aggravated offence.
(iii) Section 28 of the Crime and Disorder Act 1998 shall have effect as if the person to whom the property belongs or is treated as belonging for the purposes of the Criminal Damage Act 1971 were the victim of the offence.
(iv) For the racially or racially/religiously wordings see offence wordings H2078 and H4729.
(v) If this offence is tried by a Crown Court, it is open to the jury to return a lesser charge of simple criminal damage. In R v Fennell (2000) the point was raised that if the damage was under £5000 the offence is treated as summary and the Crown Court have no jurisdiction. However, F was unsuccessful, the offence is still either way and the Crown Court can deal with such a matter.

other.penalty:
SUMMARY: Six months imprisonment and / or a fine not exceeding the statutory maximum.
INDICTMENT: Fourteen years imprisonment and / or a fine.

Time limit for prosecutions:
None
